summary: Trajan is a Feld design built around a mancala-style tableau where picking up and redistributing pieces from one of six bowls determines which action you take, forcing players to plan several turns ahead to line up the actions they actually want. It's a classic 'salad bowl' Euro where you're juggling six semi-independent mini-games at once, each feeding a different scoring track.
praised: clever and unusual mancala action-selection mechanism
tight, satisfying puzzle of planning your bowl rotations
good replayability from the modular board and tile setups
efficient runtime for the strategic depth
criticised: thematically dry — feels like an abstract puzzle wearing a Roman skin
salad-bowl scoring can feel disconnected and hard to evaluate mid-game
steep learning curve for the mancala action system
some tracks feel stronger than others depending on tile draws

interaction.kind: drafting shared tiles and competing for senate/track position
interaction.detail: Players draft from shared forum tiles and race up common tracks (like the Senate), so there is real competition for limited resources and position, but most of the actual play happens on each player's own bowl tableau. Direct attacks or blocking of opponents is rare.

scoring.why: Trajan is a textbook Feld 'point salad': the mancala-style action selection feeds six largely independent tracks (building, trading, forum tiles, military, senate, Trajan tableau), each converting into VP in its own way.
scoring.how_you_win: Cycle pieces between the six bowls of your tableau to trigger building, trading, military, senate, forum, and Trajan-tile actions, advancing on their respective tracks and cashing in tribune/province cards; the player with the highest combined score from all these tracks at game end wins.

similar: In the Year of the Dragon
